newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hongkong Telecom swaps China shareholder.
newsitem.headline: Hongkong Telecom swaps China shareholder.

text.p: CITIC Pacific Ltd ended months of speculation about a new China partner for Hongkong Telecom by announcing on Friday the sale of its 7.74 percent stake to China-controlled China Everbright Holdings Co Ltd.
The Hong Kong-based conglomerate said it had reached a preliminary deal to sell its 904,686,181 Hongkong Telecom shares for about HK$11.4 billion ($1.47 billion) in cash.

"It has been agreed in principle that the price will be calculated on the basis of HK$12.60 per Telecom share cum dividend," CITIC Pacific said. Talks were still proceeding and no agreement had yet been signed, it added.
British-based Cable & Wireless, which owns 58.5 percent of Hongkong Telecom, appeared happy with the deal.
"We welcome the proposed investment by China Everbright in Hongkong Telecom," said Brian Smith, chairman of Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd and Cable & Wireless group
"This substantial investment of Chinese State capital demonstrates continued confidence in Hongkong Telecom and Hong Kong through the 1997 transition and beyond," he said.
Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
Analysts were less enthusiastic about the deal, however.
Investors had furiously bid up the shares of Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd this week hoping for a deal with an influential Chinese partner.
But China Everbright emerged from out of the blue.
"This certainly is just an anticlimactic development," said Andrew Fernow, director of research at Vickers Ballas. "It was simply the transfer from one passive shareholder to another."

The holding company is controlled by China's State Council and has three listed units in Hong Kong - China Everbright International Ltd, China Everbright Technology Ltd and China Everbright-IHD Pacific Ltd
CITIC Pacific's parent, China International Trust & Investment Corp, is also controlled by the State Council.
China Everbright and China International Trust & Investment both have an equal stake in China's second telephone network China United Telecommunications Corp (Unicom).
"There is nothing more strategically that China Everbright brings to the table," said Morgan Stanley analyst Jeff Camp.
One analyst, who declined to be named, said China Everbright brought little in terms of assets but had connections.

Its chairman, Zhu Xiaohua, was a deputy governor of the People's Bank of China and the deputy director of the economics department at the Hong Kong branch of Xinhua news agency prior to joining the China Everbright group in July 1996.
Analysts had expected Cable & Wireless to be involved in a deal which could have brought in China's powerful Ministry of Post and Telecommunications.

They said Hongkong Telecom was still likely to be looking for a strategic partner because mainland regulations restrict foreign companies from direct participation in China's telecommunications market.

Analysts said CITIC Pacific was the ultimate winner. It had been expected to sell its Hongkong Telecom stake after it cut its holding to eight percent from 10 percent in June last year and said it had decided to refocus its investment strategy.
"After the completion of the disposal, the company will have no further interests in Telecom shares," CITIC Pacific said.
Analysts said CITIC Pacific should get a hefty windfall from the sale -- an exceptional gain of about HK$4.00 billion -- freeing it from pressing financial needs and boosting earnings.
Its shares surged HK$0.90 in afternoon trade to close at HK$44.40. Trading in both CITIC Pacific and Hongkong Telecom shares had been suspended on Friday morning.
But after a rise of HK$1.80, or 13.6 percent this week ahead of the trading suspension, Hongkong Telecom shares closed down HK$0.50 at HK$14.50 after rising to a high of HK$15.90. ($1=HK$7.745)
